email.body1:
Jimmy, saw Aurora tripled its driverless network to 10 routes, crossed 250,000 driverless miles, and signed McLane and Hirschbach for 500 trucks.

Scaling commercial that fast usually means more carrier and shipper accounts in play than the team can cover before reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount, 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Aurora off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing those progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Jimmy, quick follow-up for Aurora.

With an $80M run-rate target and trucks rolling off the line weekly, expectations on pipeline jump faster than headcount can. Most teams don't know how many meetings they need to book to hit the number, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Aurora needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Jimmy, last bit of proof for Aurora.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Aurora's reply rate likely compares to other commercializing deep-tech companies. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Jimmy, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. A commercial ramp is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a logistics go-to-market? I'll tailor it to Aurora either way.
